title: Anchor credibility anecdote cards (draft)
body:
Purpose: quick, credible micro-anecdotes and speaker cues sellers can drop into a 60- to 180-second conversation. Not a polished deck — a pocket binder of human stories + measurable signals we can use to anchor trust when buyers ask about reliability, cost, or compliance.

How to use these cards: pick 1 persona, pick 1 objection, choose an anecdote + 1 metric line, deliver 15–45s, then offer a doc or demo. Practice with roleplay.

Target personas: platform engineer, integration architect, product manager, procurement/CFO, security/compliance lead.

Format for each card: headline (1 line), 20–40s anecdote, 1–2 raw signals (latency, cost, SLA), suggested 30s script (SE -> buyer), quick follow-up artifact to send.

Cards:
1) "Fintech trade desk: latency fallback saved a pilot"
- Anecdote: Small fintech (cleared trade desk) ran live pricing models; during spikes the hosted variant briefly hit soft limits. We enabled a policy routing fallback to a dedicated smaller quantized variant. The app stayed within 75ms p95 and we avoided a multi-hour pilot pause.
- Signals: p95 latency reduced from roughly 320ms to 78ms after routing and KV prefix cache; pilot cost delta: +9% but uptime preserved.
- Script: "When their pricing pipeline had bursty loads, we routed a portion of requests to a cheaper quantized variant while preserving latency SLAs. It cost them a few percent more in compute but saved the pilot — net ROI was retention of their 3-month pilot users.
Would you like the short trace and config we used?"
- Follow-up: send trace screenshot + routing policy snippet (link).

2) "Regulated legal automation: private deploy + audit logs"
- Anecdote: LegalTech provider needed on-prem or VPC for NDAed doc summarization. We shipped a Private deployment with KMS integration and full request audit logs. They completed a SOC-2 mapping exercise within 5 business days and signed an annual contract.
- Signals: KMS + HSM support, 90-day audit retention option (customer chose 365d), signed annual value: $420k ARR.
- Script: "For teams with strict data residency, we mapped their compliance matrix to a Private deployment, handed over an audit log extract, and ran the SOC-2 playbook with their auditor in under a week. If compliance is a blocker for you, we can do the same — I can email the template we delivered.
Shall I add you to the compliance checklist thread?"
- Follow-up: SOC-2 playbook PDF + checklist link.

3) "Marketplace search re-rank: cost per query drop with caching"
- Anecdote: Two-sided marketplace used embedding reranks on 2k QPS during peak search. We recommended local prefix caching + a micro-batch setting and a mid-quantized model for cold paths. They saw per-query cost drop by ~37% and the top-5 relevance metric stayed within 0.7% of baseline.
- Signals: 37% cost drop, latency impact: median unchanged, tail improved slightly.
- Script: "We tuned batching and enabled a short-lived prefix cache for popular queries — that cut their per-query spend by a third while keeping relevance. If you have repeat requests on the same keys, caching almost always helps. Want the caching param set we used?"
- Follow-up: send caching snippet + before/after cost graph.

4) "Healthcare intake triage: deterministic fallbacks for hallucination risk"
- Anecdote: Pilot at a healthcare SaaS used structured tool calling to avoid free-form summaries in clinical triage. We enforced a schema-first output with a canary model in the loop. That reduced hallucination flags by ~82% in human moderation checks.
- Signals: hallucination flags fell from 11% to 2%, human-review time down 44%.
- Script: "For high-risk workflows we push structured outputs and a canary checking pass. It caught issues early and cut moderation load. If your team needs deterministic outputs we can show a small demo with structured tool calls.
Do you want a quick demo next week?"
- Follow-up: demo recording + prompt template.

5) "Retail personalization: reserved capacity smoothing"
- Anecdote: Retail brand preparing a flash sale feared capacity cliffs. We recommended a minimal Dedicated reservation with autoscale headroom plus a burst policy. During the sale, they hit 1.4x baseline traffic but never degraded; checkout conversions remained steady.
- Signals: conversion delta: +0.3% vs expected; no SLA violations; reserved plan costed ~18% more than ephemeral but prevented lost revenue.
- Script: "Reserved capacity buys predictability in revenue windows — we modeled their margin and showed reserved spend was cheaper than lost conversions during peak. I can run that ARPU model for your sale.
Want me to run a quick forecast?"
- Follow-up: 1-pager model + cost vs revenue graph.

6) "Platform migration: canary rollout + rollback policy wins"
- Anecdote: Platform team migrating an internal chatbot used A/B canary rollouts with automatic fallback to previous model and a degradation alert pipeline. A problematic model variant was automatically rolled back within 3 minutes with no customer-facing errors.
- Signals: MTTR for bad rollout < 3min, rollback success rate 100% in tests.
- Script: "We recommend canary policies with automated rollbacks triggered by a delta in error rates or latency. That way, bad model pushes never become product issues. Want the canary config we use?"
- Follow-up: canary policy excerpt + monitoring dashboard links.

Quick rebuttal bank (short lines you can say mid-conversation):
- "We treat caching and routing as first-class levers — same request, cheaper path, no code changes."
- "Private deployments are just our control plane in a private network; you still get the same rollout and observability tools."
- "We quantify fallback cost vs lost revenue in pilot — it's rarely the cheapest compute path that wins, it's the one that preserves customer flows."

Slide/mini-deck outline (for a 6-slide 3-minute seller deck):
- Slide 1: 30s opener + trust hook (one line from a card and a metric)
- Slide 2: Problem frames by persona (bullet per persona)
- Slide 3: Three short customer anecdotes (cards 1,2,3) with one metric each
- Slide 4: Ops knobs we pull (routing, caching, quantization, private deploy) + tiny icons
- Slide 5: Roleplay script live demo (30s)
- Slide 6: Next steps + artifacts to drop (checklist + links)

Rehearsal cues for SEs (do this in the first 60s):
- Quick intro: "I help platform engineering teams get predictable inference economics and keep apps online when models and traffic move."
- Early trust anchor: "We recently helped a legal workflow finish a SOC-2 mapping in 5 days — I can share the checklist."
- Short pause after the metric; ask: "Does that sound like a win for you?"

Roleplay snippet (SE / Buyer)
- SE: "When your search traffic spikes, do you currently have a fallback policy?"
- Buyer: "Not a formal one — we scale more infra, but it's costly."
- SE: "We typically enable routing to a quantized variant for non-critical requests and caching for repeat queries. It reduces spend and keeps tail latency bounded. If you want, I can map this to your QPS — takes 20 minutes."

Open questions / TODOs (internal):
- Collect 2–3 short screenshots: routing policy diff, trace from fintech pilot, SOC-2 checklist extract.
- Validate the $420k ARR number with finance and swap with redacted real value if needed. (Priya)
- Create a one-click artifact pack (PDF + 3 images) sellers can email after a meeting. (Liam)
- Record a 90s demo showing routing + canary rollback in sandbox. (Ethan)

Notes to self / voice: keep it human, not too many stats in the opener, prioritize story + 1 metric. This is stackable — sellers should carry 2–3 cards in their head and 1 artifact link in the follow-up.

Links to templates and snippets to attach in follow-up email: conf://INFER-ANECDOTES-2025, https://imgur.com/redwood-samples/cost-graph, https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1-example-artifact-pack

End of draft.

(Last edit notes: cleaned up phrasing, added healthcare card and a Canaries card; still draft — will swap in finalized metrics after finance sign-off.)
